title: V is for VOR: Stop relying on your flight screen! | MSFS A-Z
description:
Following a bright magenta line on a modern flight screen is easy, but there's a completely different level of satisfaction that comes from turning off the GPS, looking out at a blanket of clouds, and knowing exactly where you are in the world using nothing but radio waves. Welcome back to our Microsoft Flight Simulator A-Z series! Today, we’ve reached the letter V, and we are mastering the art of VOR navigation.

Many beginners feel completely lost the moment they turn off the moving map. In this episode, we break down the simple "radio lighthouse" physics behind ground-based beacons, decode the confusing symbols on your flight chart, and transition you from a casual simmer following a computer screen to a true pilot who can navigate a classic aircraft coast to coast completely by hand.

In this video, you’ll discover:

- The radio lighthouse analogy: How analog timing calculates your exact celestial highway.
- Hexagons, squares, and stars: How to instantly identify VOR, VOR-DME, and VORTAC stations.
- The golden rule: A step-by-step application of the "Tune, Identify, Twist" workflow.
- Ultimate pro skill: How to pinpoint an invisible crossroad in the sky using dual navigation radios.

🕒 Chapters
00:00 - Intro
00:39 - The core concept
01:31 - The 3 chart symbols
02:16 - Understanding the instrument face
03:43 - The golden rule
04:01 - The beginner method: tuning & flying outbound
14:45 - The advanced method: the Schiphol intersection

Whether you are flying a vintage piston aircraft or looking to backup your modern glass cockpit during an electronics failure, mastering radio navigation is what separates desk-simmers from true virtual aviators.
